land.text: the Garonne valley of Gallia Aquitania, granted by Honorius to the Visigothic federates under Wallia in 418

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's first Visigothic shape begins in 426; the infobox of the Visigothic Kingdom page says 'Established: 418'.

land.text: the peninsula and Septimania conquered by the Umayyads 711-721 (Visigothic Kingdom page: 'Most of the Visigothic Kingdom was conquered by Umayyad troops from North Africa in 711 to 719'; Septimania occupied 721)

successors.note: Cliopatria's Umayyad row begins 656; the Umayyad dossier (me-07) should show the land as taken 711-721.

land.text: the unconquered north: Pelagius 'revolted in 718, and defeated the Muslims at the battle of Covadonga' (Visigothic Kingdom page; the Umayyad page dates Covadonga 722)

successors.note: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Asturias row begins in 724. Cliopatria's 718-723 Visigothic shape still draws Galicia, Asturias and Cantabria as Visigothic; this dossier gives them to Asturias.

capitals.name: Toledo
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Toledo (542-711)'. After 711 the page names no seat for the Septimanian rump under Ardo (714-721); none is invented here.

rulers.name: Wallia
rulers.note: Page list 415-418 (king from 415, before this state's first year); the state's first year is 418 (Honorius's grant), so his entry starts in 418. [Reviewer eu-06-d: from 415 to 418, rulers must lie inside the life.]

rulers.name: Thorismund
rulers.note: Page: family list only.

rulers.name: Theodoric II
rulers.note: Murdered by Euric in 466 (Theodoric II page).

rulers.name: Alaric II
rulers.note: Killed at Vouillé, 507.

rulers.name: Gesalec
rulers.note: Deposed and killed after trying to counter-strike at Narbonne (Vouillé page).

rulers.name: Theodoric the Great
rulers.title: regent
rulers.note: Regent for the infant Amalaric (Theodoric the Great page: Visigothic Kingdom 'brought under Theodoric's direct control' in 511).

rulers.name: Amalaric
rulers.note: Page gives 511-531; he reigned under Theodoric's regency to 526.

rulers.name: Athanagild
rulers.note: Page gives 552-568 in the text and 554-568 in the list; the Athanagild page infobox gives March 554 to December 567.

rulers.name: Liuva I
rulers.note: Co-king with Liuvigild from 569 (page list 568-572).

rulers.name: Liuvigild
rulers.note: Liuvigild page: 569/568 to 21 April 586; sole ruler from Liuva's death.

rulers.name: Sisebut
rulers.note: Infobox and list 612-621; text 612-620.

rulers.name: Suintila
rulers.note: Expelled the last Byzantine garrisons in 624.

rulers.name: Recceswinth
rulers.note: Infobox and list 649-672 (co-ruler from 649); text 653-672. Visigothic Code 654.

rulers.name: Wittiza
rulers.note: Page list and infobox 694-710 (co-ruler with Egica from 694).

rulers.name: Roderic
rulers.note: Defeated at the Guadalete, July 711.

rulers.name: Agila II
rulers.note: List only (the Umayyad page names the successor 'Achila II' and dates the last king Ardo from 713 or 714).

rulers.name: Ardo
rulers.note: Last king; Septimania the last area under effective Visigothic control; died 721 (Umayyad page).

correction.text: the Garonne valley of Gallia Aquitania around Toulouse, the land Honorius granted to Wallia's federates in 418

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Visigothic shape starts in 426, the page says 'Established: 418'. The 426 shape (140 cells, all inside the Aquitaine region, 35,100 km2) is read as the Garonne-valley grant. No infobox area for this date to compare.

35,100 km2 around Toulouse; the page gives no area for 426. Theodoric I 'completed the settlements of the Visigoths in Gallia Aquitania II, Novempopulana, and Gallia Narbonensis' (Theodoric I page, undated), so the shape is a minimum for 426-454.

correction.text: shape unchanged but for 455 only; 456-458 are the Spanish occupation shown by the 458 shape

keyframe_review.note: 73,560 km2: Aquitaine plus the first Narbonensis edge. Theodoric II's army, after the Battle of the Orbigo (456), 'controlled the Spanish provinces Hispania Baetica', most of Tarraconensis and southern Lusitania, so the Spanish reach belongs from 456 (the 458 shape), not 455 alone.

correction.text: shape unchanged; years 456-458 rather than 458 alone

keyframe_review.note: 569,232 km2 for one year: Aquitaine plus Baetica, most of Tarraconensis and southern Lusitania, without Galicia (gazetteer check: 1742 Hispania cells, Galicia 0), which is what the Theodoric II page describes 'after 456'. The page does not date the withdrawal ('the Goths abandoned their settlements in Spain and returned to Aquitaine' after Majorian's victory at Arles); Cliopatria's 459 shape has them gone. The shape should hold 456-458.
73,467 km2: Aquitaine again after the Spanish withdrawal; Narbonne is added in 461 (next shape).

112,893 km2: Aquitaine plus Narbonne and its surroundings, 'In 461, the Goths received the city of Narbonne from the emperor Libius Severus'. Theodoric II page: south of the Loire taken after Aegidius withdrew in 461, but the shape stops at 46.3 N, so that claim is not drawn.

correction.text: the 469 shape without Berry (taken 471) and Auvergne (Clermont surrendered 475)

keyframe_review.note: 591,755 km2: the whole peninsula except Galicia and the north-east, plus Aquitaine to the Loire, Berry and Auvergne. Pages: Merida 469 (Visigothic Kingdom page), Berry 471 and the battle near Arles 471, 'in 472 he conquered most of Hispania', Clermont 475 (Euric page). So Berry and Auvergne enter 2-6 years after the shape draws them; the 469 shape is right for 469-470 minus Berry and Auvergne.

correction.text: the 469 shape without Auvergne, where 'only by strong resistance in Auvergne, the center of Gaul, could the Romans stand against him'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 471-474, the 469 shape with Berry (471, after the victory near Arles) but without Auvergne (Clermont 475) and with Tarraconensis (472).
New keyframe for the single year 475: Clermont surrenders 'after a long siege' and Nepos recognises Euric's independence, so Auvergne is inside; the shape is Cliopatria's 469 shape unchanged.

correction.text: the 476 shape with Provence, which the Euric page has Nepos renounce in 475

keyframe_review.note: 669,591 km2: adds the Barcelona region to the 469 shape. Euric page: Nepos 'renounced Provence in 475, as well as the region around Barcelona to Euric'; Visigothic Kingdom page: 'By 476, he had extended his rule to the Rhone and the Loire'. The two pages disagree on whether Provence (east of the Rhone) was inside in 476; Cliopatria adds it only in 480. The shape follows the Euric page (475).

689,151 km2 against the infobox's 500,000 km2 for 484 (ratio 1.38, inside the factor of two). Euric's death in 484: 'the Kingdom of the Visigoths encompassed a third of modern France' and 'almost all of Iberia' except Galicia held by the Suebi.

689,712 km2, the maximum. Vouillé (spring 507) took Aquitaine and Toulouse and 'By 508 the Visigoths had lost most of their Gallic holdings save Septimania' (Visigothic Kingdom page), but Cliopatria keeps the full shape to 509: right for 490-506, then the 507 keyframe applies.

correction.text: Hispania and Septimania, 'the Visigoths had lost most of their Gallic holdings save Septimania' by 508

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 507-509, the Visigothic Kingdom after Vouillé: the peninsula and Septimania, the Gallic north and Provence gone. Cliopatria's 510 shape (480,655 km2) is used three years earlier than it starts.

480,655 km2: the peninsula plus Septimania; the shape stays almost unchanged to 554. The page gives no infobox area for these years (484: 500,000 km2 and 580: 600,000 km2 are compared at the 480 and 577 shapes).
481,199 km2. No territorial change on the pages for 523-533 (Theodoric the Great regent to 526; Amalaric to 531). The 5-cell flicker against the 510 shape is boundary noise.
481,584 km2. Unverified: page budget; no territorial event on the pages for 534-539 (Theudis 531-548).
481,538 km2. Toledo becomes the capital in 542 (infobox). Unverified: page budget for any change inside the shape.

399,429 km2: the south coast (Cadiz-Malaga-Almeria-Cartagena) drops out. Spania page: Byzantines 'occupied many coastal cities in Baetica' after 555; the province dates 'from 552 until 624'; 'By the year 600 Spania had dwindled to little more than Malaga and Cartagena and the Balearics'.
403,534 km2: +19 coastal cells around Cadiz in the south-west; unverified: page budget (the Spania page gives no change in 567).

403,477 km2. Liuvigild's southern campaigns begin 570 (Bastetania and Malaga laid waste), Medina Sidonia 571, Cordoba 571/572; the Cliopatria jump to 438,274 km2 comes in 577. The 569 shape is right only for 569-570.

correction.text: the 577 shape with Medina Sidonia and Cordoba, taken from the Byzantines 571-572

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 571-576, the 577 shape moved five years earlier: Medina Sidonia (571), Cordoba (571 or 572) and the south-west. Orospeda (south-east, 577) is part of the 577 shape and cannot be separated here.

correction.text: shape unchanged; years 577-579, then the Baetica revolt (580-584) and the Suebi conquest (585) change it

keyframe_review.note: 438,274 km2 against the infobox's 600,000 km2 for 580 (Cliopatria/infobox ratio 0.73, inside the factor of two; the shape still lacks Galicia): adds Orospeda (577: 'marched into Orospeda, a region in southeastern Spain') on top of the 571 gains. Hermenegild's revolt holds Baetica 580-584 (ledger), so the shape is right for 577-579 only; 585 adds the Suebi.

New keyframe: 585-586, 'In 585, Liuvigild conquered the Suebi peoples'; Cliopatria draws Galicia as Visigothic only from 587. Liuvigild at his death (586): only 'the Basque lands and two small southern territories of the Byzantine Empire' were non-Visigothic.
529,343 km2 (ratio 0.88 to the infobox's 600,000 km2 for 580): the peninsula with Galicia; the Basque lands and Malaga-Cartagena excluded.
531,255 km2 (+12 cells in the south-east). Spania page: 'Baza was Visigothic by 589'. Unverified: page budget for the rest.

550,773 km2: +80 cells on the northern coast (Cantabria, Asturias, Burgos). The Duchy of Cantabria page dates the destruction of Amaya and the City of Cantabria to 574; Cliopatria draws the northern strip as it stands from 602. Unverified: page budget for the 592-612 northern increments (the Vascones page gives no Visigothic dates).
561,284 km2 (+48 cells in the north). Unverified: page budget. Sisebut's two expeditions of 614-615 conquered Malaga 'before 619' (Spania page), which this shape does not yet include.

correction.text: shape unchanged; years 624-660 (Balearics still nominally Byzantine)

keyframe_review.note: 603,537 km2: the south coast returns. Spania page: 'by 624 the entire province of Spania was in Visigothic hands save the Balearic Islands' (a footnote gives 625 or 629 for the last vestiges); Suintila 'recovered' the last towns held in 621. The shape starts a year early and Malaga came earlier (before 619).

578,862 km2: loses 100 cells in the Rioja-Navarre-Aragon Pyrenean belt (lat 42-43.5 N, lon 4 W to 2 E). No page opened dates a Visigothic loss there: the Vascones page records only 'repeated conflicts between the Vascones and the Visigoths and Franks' and independence 'at least until the campaign of Leovigild'. Unverified: page budget.
578,910 km2, unchanged in substance.

correction.text: shape unchanged; years 710-713, with the ledger's losses applied 711-714

keyframe_review.note: 578,868 km2: the full peninsula is right only until the Guadalete (July 711). The Umayyads took Merida (mid-summer 712), Seville, Cordoba and Toledo (712), Leon, Astorga and Zaragoza (713); the ledger removes the land year by year.

correction.text: Septimania, the last area under effective Visigothic control, 714-721

keyframe_review.note: 99,971 km2 for 718-723: Septimania plus Galicia, Asturias and Cantabria. The Umayyad page: 'Septimania the last area under effective Visigothic control' under Ardo (713/714-721), Narbonne fell 719 or 720; the north-west coast is Pelagius's Asturias (revolt 718 on the Visigothic page, Covadonga 722 on the Umayyad page). The Visigothic remnant is Septimania, 714-721.

ledger.note: 418: Honorius settles the Visigoths under Wallia in the Garonne valley of Gallia Aquitania. 'In 418, Honorius rewarded his Visigothic federates under King Wallia (reigned 415-418) by giving them land in the Garonne valley of Gallia Aquitania'; infobox 'Established: 418'; capital Toulouse 418-507.

region.text: the growth from the 426 shape to the 455 shape: Aquitania II, Novempopulana and the Narbonensis edge

ledger.note: 451: the settlements spread over Aquitania II, Novempopulana and Narbonensis. Theodoric I (418-451) 'completed the settlements of the Visigoths in Gallia Aquitania II, Novempopulana, and Gallia Narbonensis'; the page does not date the steps, so the year is the end of his reign (a bridging date). Cliopatria's 455 shape is the result.

region.text: Baetica, most of Tarraconensis and southern Lusitania, without Galicia

ledger.note: 456: the Goths take the Spanish provinces after the Orbigo. Theodoric II 'defeated him in the Battle of Orbigo (456)', took Braga, and his army 'controlled the Spanish provinces Hispania Baetica', most of Tarraconensis and southern Lusitania; 'In Spain he left soldier colonies'. The page does not say who held each province (the Suebi held the north-west).

459: the Goths leave Spain. 'The Goths abandoned their settlements in Spain and returned to Aquitaine' after Majorian's victory at Arles; the page gives no year, so 459 is Cliopatria's (shape 459) and a bridging date.

region.text: the city of Narbonne and its surroundings

ledger.note: 461: Narbonne. 'In 461, the Goths received the city of Narbonne from the emperor Libius Severus.' The Theodoric II page adds that after Aegidius withdrew north of the Loire 'the area south of it was taken by Theoderic' (not drawn in Cliopatria's 462 shape).

region.text: the peninsula without Galicia and the north-east, added in the 469 shape

ledger.note: 469: Merida and the west of the peninsula. 'taking Emerita Augusta (Merida) in 469'; the Euric page, on the crisis of 468 after the defeat of the Roman fleet: 'The cities of Merikda, Braga, Zaragona, Pamploma and Cluna were occupied or armed' (its spellings; it does not identify Merikda with Merida). Cliopatria draws most of the peninsula in 469, the Euric page only 'most of Hispania' in 472.

471: Berry and a foothold in Provence. After the victory near Arles 'which enabled him to conquer the area of Berry'; 'Euric got a strong foothold in Provence'. His Gallic push north of the Loire failed near Orleans in 469.

region.text: most of Hispania Tarraconensis, without the north-east round Barcelona (475)

ledger.note: 472: Tarraconensis. 'capturing Hispania Tarraconensis in 472'; the Euric page: 'In 472 he conquered most of Hispania. Only the northeast, with the city of Barcelona as centrum remained in Roman hands.'
475: Clermont and Auvergne. 'In the same year, Clermont(-Ferrand) surrendered to him after a long siege.'

475: Nepos gives up the Barcelona region. 'Nepos renounced Provence in 475, as well as the region around Barcelona to Euric'; Euric forced him to recognise full independence, the Visigothic Kingdom page: 'signed in 475 an alliance with Euric'.

475: Provence. 'Nepos renounced Provence in 475'; the same page also words it 'in exchange for the return of the Provence region'; the Visigothic Kingdom page gives only 'the Rhone and the Loire' for 476, so the boundary is uncertain. Cliopatria adds Provence only in 480.

region.text: Gallia Aquitania, conquered by the Franks after Vouillé

ledger.note: 507: Vouillé. 'Alaric II was killed at the Battle of Campus Vogladensis (Vouillé) near Poitiers, and Toulouse was sacked' (Visigothic Kingdom page); the Franks gained 'the southwestern part of France' and 'the conquest of Gallia Aquitania' (Vouillé page: 'around spring 507').
507: the court leaves Toulouse for Barcelona, 'temporarily' (infobox: Barcelona 507-542).

region.text: the Gallic holdings north and east of Aquitaine

ledger.note: 508: the rest of Gaul but Septimania. 'By 508, the Visigoths had lost most of their Gallic holdings save Septimania in the south.' The Vouillé page adds that Narbonne 'was taken by Burgundian allies of the Franks' and that Gesalec's counterstrike at Narbonne failed; it is silent on which holdings went to whom, so the Auvergne-Berry-Loire reading and the Frankish counterpart are mine.

510: Provence leaves the Visigothic shape. 'starting in 508, Theodoric's generals campaigned in Gaul' and 'in 510 Theodoric reestablished the defunct praetorian prefecture of Gaul'; but the page says this was 'at the expense of the Burgundians', not the Visigoths, and does not name Arles or Marseille. The Euric page has Provence Visigothic since 475, so the handover is a bridging reading.

511: Gesalec is deposed and Theodoric the Great takes the Visigothic Kingdom under his direct control as regent for his grandson Amalaric. 'In 511, the Visigothic Kingdom was brought under Theodoric's direct control, forming a Gothic superstate that extended from the Atlantic to the Danube.' The Ostrogothic dossier should carry the vassal tint 511-526; the Balthi line resumes with Amalaric.
542: the capital moves from Barcelona to Toledo (infobox: 'Toledo (542-711)').

region.text: Seville, held by Athanagild against Agila

ledger.note: 551: Athanagild takes Seville. 'He had rebelled against his predecessor, Agila I, in 551' (Athanagild page); the Spania page: 'a nobleman named Athanagild took Seville', 'Either at the commencement of his reign (549) or as late as 551'. The page names Seville, not the province.

region.text: Seville and the land the rebels held

ledger.note: 554: Agila dies and Athanagild is sole ruler, so the rebel land rejoins the kingdom. 'Following the death of Agila in 554, he was sole ruler' (the Spania page dates Agila's murder to late March 555; the infobox of the Athanagild page gives his reign from March 554).

region.text: the south coast of Baetica and Carthaginiensis (Cadiz to Cartagena)

ledger.note: 555: the Byzantine province of Spania. The imperial army 'was probably sent in 552'; 'landed at Cartagena in early March 555 and marched inland to Baza'; the Byzantines then 'occupied many coastal cities in Baetica', a province held 'from 552 until 624'.
569: Liuvigild's first campaign against the Suebi. 'his first campaign began against the Suebi in 569, during which he very quickly subdued Zamora, Palencia, and Leon.'

571: Medina Sidonia. 'The following year he captured Medina Sidonia, assisted through the treachery of a certain Framidaneus' (the Spania page: held by the Byzantines until reconquered by Leovigild in 572).

572: Cordoba. 'seized Cordoba from the Byzantine Empire' (Liuvigild page: 571 or 572); the Spania page: 'in a state of rebellion... until Leovigild put it down in 572' and calls its Byzantine status disputed.

union.text: the City of Cantabria, believed near Logrono

region.text: Amaya and the City of Cantabria

ledger.note: 574: Amaya and the City of Cantabria destroyed. 'Both towns were destroyed in 574 by Liuvigild, who massacred many of their inhabitants.' The Liuvigild page has the capture of 'Ammaia, the capital of the Cantabri' in 576. Amaya is in northern Burgos, the City of Cantabria believed near Logrono.
577: Orospeda. 'He marched into Orespeda, a region in southeastern Spain' and added it to the kingdom; the Spania page: 'a region under Byzantine control'.

580: Baetica rises under Hermenegild. 'He fell out with his father in 579, then revolted the following year' (Hermenegild page); the Liuvigild page: 'Baetica revolted under the leadership of Hermenegild', 579-584.
582: Merida. Liuvigild 'captured Merida', which had been under Bishop Masona's control since the early 570s.

584: Seville falls and the revolt ends. 'Hermenegild fled to Seville and when it fell to a siege in 584, he went to Cordoba' (Hermenegild page); Liuvigild 'besieged and took Seville'. Hermenegild was executed on 13 April 585.
585: the Suebi kingdom is conquered. 'In 585, Liuvigild conquered the Suebi peoples, bringing an end to some forty-years of their independence in Spain.'

region.text: the northern coast of Cantabria, Asturias and Burgos

ledger.note: 602: the northern strip fills in. Cliopatria adds 80 cells on the Cantabrian coast and in Burgos between 592 and 602. No page opened dates it (the Vascones page is silent on Visigothic campaigns; Liuvigild 'pacified northern Spain but was unable to completely conquer' the Basques). A bridging date.

region.text: the north, Cantabria and La Rioja

ledger.note: 612: the northern strip fills in further. Cliopatria adds 48 cells in the north between 602 and 612; no page opened dates it. A bridging date.
615: Malaga. 'In 614 and 615, he carried out two massive expeditions against them and conquered Malaga before 619' (Sisebut).

region.text: the south coast of Baetica and Carthaginiensis, Cadiz to Cartagena

ledger.note: 624: the Byzantines are expelled from the peninsula. 'until 624 when Swinthila expelled the last Byzantine garrisons'; infobox 'Conquest of Byzantine Spania: 624' (the same page says 625 elsewhere, a Spania footnote 625 or 629). The Balearics stayed nominally Byzantine.
661: the Pyrenean belt of the Ebro and Rioja leaves the shape. Cliopatria drops 100 cells there between 623 and 661; no page opened dates a Visigothic loss. A bridging date.

711: the Umayyads land and win the Guadalete. Tariq ibn Ziyad 'lands with 400 men and 100 horses on the tiny peninsula now called Gibraltar' (710/711); 'King Roderic's army utterly routed in the Battle of Guadalete', 'in July that year' (the Visigothic Kingdom page: 'By late July, a battle took place at the Guadalete River in the province of Cadiz').
712: Merida falls. Merida 'was ultimately conquered in mid-summer 712'.

712: Seville, Cordoba and Toledo. Seville was 'rapidly captured' by the second invasion of 712; 'Some towns (Cordova, Toledo, etc.) were stormed and captured unconditionally', which the page does not date; 712 is the year of the second invasion.

region.text: Galicia, the north-east and the south-east

ledger.note: 713: Leon, Astorga and Zaragoza. 'The following year the combined forces continued into Galicia and the northeast, capturing Leon, Astorga and Zaragoza.' The Treaty of Theodemir (713) is indirect rule over the south-east.

region.text: what is left of the peninsula but the mountains of the north

ledger.note: 714: the rest of the peninsula. Musa 'headed north-west up the Ebro river to overrun the western Basque regions'; 'As of 713 (or 714), the last Visigothic king, Ardo' ruled only Septimania.
714: the fighting for the south and centre ends; the Umayyads hold the peninsula but for the mountains of the north and Ardo's Septimania ('As of 713 (or 714), the last Visigothic king, Ardo').
717: the first Umayyad forays into Septimania, under al-Hurr ibn Abd al-Rahman.
720: Narbonne falls. The timeline lists Narbonne captured in 719, the body says 'Narbonne fell (720)'.
721: Ardo dies and Septimania passes to the Umayyads. 'King Ardo died (721)'; the infobox lists 'Umayyad occupation of Septimania: 721', and the text takes it 'between 721 and 725'.

721: the Visigothic Kingdom ends with Ardo and the fall of Septimania; 'Most of the Visigothic Kingdom was conquered by Umayyad troops from North Africa in 711 to 719'. Pelagius's Asturias survives in the north (Covadonga 718 or 722).

wars.name: Gothic attacks on Narbonne and Toulouse
wars.outcome: Theodoric I's attack on Narbonne in 436 was stopped by Litorius, who drove the Goths back to Toulouse; 'in 439 at the Battle of Toulouse the Visigoths defeated the allied forces of Romans and Huns'. No land changed hands.
wars.note: Theodoric I page: 'Theodoric saw the chance to conquer Narbo Martius in 436'; the Toulouse battle is undated there and 439 on the Visigothic Kingdom page.

wars.name: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains
wars.outcome: Visigoths and Romans defeat Attila's Huns; Theodoric I is killed. No territorial result.
wars.note: 'in or about June 451'; 'Theodoric's forces contributed decisively to the victory of the Romans, but he himself was killed'.

wars.name: Visigothic campaign against the Suebi
wars.outcome: Theodoric II defeats the Suebi at the Orbigo, takes Braga and plunders Gallaecia; the Goths then hold the Spanish provinces (ledger 456). The Suebi keep Galicia until 585.

wars.name: Majorian's war against the Visigoths
wars.outcome: Majorian defeated the Goths at Arles; in the peace the Goths gave up their Spanish settlements and returned to Aquitaine.
wars.note: The Theodoric II page does not date the war ('post-457'); the years follow Cliopatria's 458-459 shapes and are a bridging reading.

wars.name: Euric's Gallic and Hispanic campaigns
wars.outcome: Euric wins the battle near Arles (471), Berry, most of Hispania (472), Clermont (475); in 475 Nepos recognises his independence and renounces Provence and the Barcelona region. His attempt on northern Gaul failed in 469.

wars.name: Battle of Vouillé

zones.text: Gallia Aquitania, conquered by the Franks after Vouillé

wars.outcome: Clovis defeats and kills Alaric II 'around spring 507'; the Franks take Aquitaine and Toulouse, the Visigoths keep Septimania.

wars.name: Visigothic civil war of Agila and Athanagild
wars.outcome: Athanagild rebels in 551, takes Seville and asks Justinian for help; the Byzantines land (552) and Agila is defeated, then dies in 554. Athanagild reigns alone; the Byzantine province of Spania remains.
wars.note: Years follow the Athanagild page (rebellion 551, Agila's death 554); the Spania page dates the revolt 549-551 and Agila's murder to March 555.

wars.name: Byzantine-Visigothic wars in Spania

zones.text: the Byzantine coast of Baetica and Carthaginiensis

wars.outcome: Spania held 552-624; Leovigild retakes Medina Sidonia and Cordoba (571-572) and Orospeda (577), Sisebut Malaga (614-615), Suintila the last towns (624).

wars.name: Liuvigild's reconquest and the Suebi

zones.text: Medina Sidonia, captured the year after 570
Córdoba, seized from the Byzantine Empire

wars.outcome: Liuvigild subdues Zamora, Palencia and Leon (569), the south (570-577), the Cantabri (574), Mérida (582) and ends the Suebic kingdom in 585.

wars.name: Revolt of Hermenegild
wars.outcome: Liuvigild takes Merida (582) and Seville (584); Hermenegild is imprisoned and executed on 13 April 585; the Byzantines withdrew after Liuvigild paid 30,000 pieces of gold.

wars.name: Umayyad conquest of Hispania
wars.outcome: Guadalete (July 711); Merida 712; Seville, Cordoba, Toledo 712; Leon, Astorga, Zaragoza 713; Ardo holds Septimania until his death in 721; Narbonne falls 719 or 720.

certainty.note: The grants of 418, 461 and 475 are by province or city, not by surveyed line; the Suebi, Basque, Cantabrian and Byzantine-coast frontiers are approximate, and the Pyrenean frontier with the Franks after 507 is a band, not a line.

notes: Cliopatria's first shape begins 426 but the pages date the kingdom to 418 (Honorius's grant), so a 418-425 keyframe was added. The end is set at 721 (Ardo's death, Septimania occupied) although Cliopatria's last shape runs to 723; its 718-723 shape (99,971 km2) draws Septimania plus Galicia, Asturias and Cantabria, and the north-west coast is given to the Kingdom of Asturias here (Cliopatria row 724); Pelagius's revolt is 718 on the Visigothic Kingdom page and Covadonga 722 on the Umayyad page. Pages that failed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Visigothic_kings (and List_of_Visigoth_kings) would not load; the ruler list is the Visigothic Kingdom article's own table, which gives two sets of years for several reigns (noted per ruler). Ten pages were opened against a budget of nine (one, Vascones, was silent on dates). Unverified: the 592-612 northern gains and the 661 loss of the Rioja-Navarre-Aragon belt are Cliopatria's with no page opened dating them (confidence 1 events); 523-554 shapes are unchanged in substance. Provence 508-510: the Ostrogothic Kingdom page has Theodoric's generals taking southern Gaul 'at the expense of the Burgundians', the Euric page has Provence Visigothic from 475; the handover to the Ostrogoths is a bridging reading (confidence 1). Rebel dossiers added: revolt-of-athanagild (551-554) and revolt-of-hermenegild (580-584). Counterparts needing dossiers: Vascones/Basques (a people, no row), the Laguatan etc. belong to the Vandal dossier. The Ostrogothic Kingdom dossier should carry a vassal tint over the Visigothic Kingdom 511-526 (the Visigothic page's own words: 'brought under Theodoric's direct control'). Small unexplained increments: +19 cells on the south-west coast in 567 and +12 cells in the south-east in 592 have no event (the pages opened are silent). Septimania 508-531: Amalaric's defeat at Narbonne (531) and Theudis's reign are not on the pages opened; the shape stays flat.
